title: Eurozone retail sales fall in July as consumer spending softens
description: Full report here Retail sales in the Eurozone declined in July, pointing to softer consumer demand. The volume of retail trade fell by 0.6% m/m in July, reversing the 0.2% increase recorded in June. Across the broader European Union, retail sales declined by 0.4% after also rising 0.2% in the previous month.  On an annual basis, however, retail activity remained slightly positive. Compared with July 2025, Eurozone retail sales increased 0.6%, while sales across the EU rose 1.0%. The monthly decline was driven primarily by weaker demand for non-food products, where sales dropped 1.4%
